items.title: Percy Heath — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Let me tell you, John Lewis set up… he knew, if he did a certain thing, what Jackson would do. They were unbelievable. I played with those people for forty years and I never heard them play the same thing twice.

ctx.x: Let me tell you, John Lewis set up… he knew, if he did a certain thing, what Jackson would do. They were unbelievable. I played with those people for forty years and I never heard them play the same thing twice. They may have the same vocabulary, but never the same thing in the same place in thousands of concerts. Thousands. They never repeated. Like the solo of “Flying Home,” if you didn’t play that solo of Illinois Jacquet, you didn’t play the tune. I don’t care what tenor player it was. If you didn’t play that…
Where the solo becomes like an arrangement.
